_readme: SAIRNlaw deadline engine seed -- Ohio and Indiana discovery response
deadlines. Phase 6.
THESE ARE THE FOUR RULES PHASE 5 REFUSED TO SEED, and they are seeded now
only because the engine gained a shape that can express them honestly.
Nothing about the rule text changed; the verified quotes below are the same
ones read on 2026-08-22 in Phase 5.
WHY THEY COULD NOT BE SEEDED BEFORE. All four read the same way:
Ohio Civ.R. 33(A)     'within a period designated by the party submitting
the interrogatories, NOT LESS THAN twenty-eight
days after the service of the interrogatories'
Ohio Civ.R. 36(A)(1)  'within a period designated in the request, NOT LESS
THAN twenty-eight days after service'
Ind. T.R. 33(C)       '...NOT LESS THAN thirty days'
Ind. T.R. 36(A)       '...NOT LESS THAN thirty days after service thereof'
The operative deadline is whatever the propounding party designated. The
number in the rule is a FLOOR on what a valid request may demand, not a
deadline. Seeding 28 or 30 as a fixed period would have put a date on
screen that is not the user's deadline whenever the request designated
longer -- which is most of the time.
HOW THEY ARE EXPRESSED NOW. Each rule carries designated_period { min,
unit, designated_by }, and count.value holds the SAME number purely as the
floor. The engine never counts from count.value for these rules; it
requires designated_period_days as input and counts from that. The endpoint
validator enforces that the two numbers match, so a row whose floor and
count disagree cannot be stored at all.
THREE REFUSALS, and the distinction between them is the point:
DESIGNATED_PERIOD_REQUIRED (422) -- no period supplied. The rule is
loaded and the request is well-formed; the engine simply has not been
told the one fact that determines the deadline. It names the floor and
who designates the period.
DESIGNATED_PERIOD_BELOW_FLOOR (400) -- a period was supplied and the rule
does not permit it. This is the only refusal in the whole engine that
says something is WRONG rather than merely absent, which is why it is a
400 rather than a 422. It reports the designated figure and the floor
side by side.
BAD_DESIGNATED_PERIOD (400) -- not a whole positive number.
WHY A BELOW-FLOOR DESIGNATION IS REFUSED RATHER THAN RAISED TO THE FLOOR.
Computing the floor instead would answer a question nobody asked and would
quietly paper over a defective request. And the further question -- whether
a request designating less than the minimum is VOID, or merely
unenforceable as to timing -- is a question of law, not of arithmetic.
This engine does not pick between them. It refuses, names the floor, and
says plainly that the point is for a human to resolve. Decided 2026-08-22
with Michael; recorded here rather than left as an implementation detail
because a future session would otherwise be tempted to make it 'more
helpful'.
NO SERVICE EXTENSION on any rule here, and the validator now blocks one
structurally for this rule shape: the designated figure already IS the
period, so adding days to a party-chosen number would extend a deadline the
rule never set. Ohio's Civ.R. 6(D) mail extension is separately carved out
for responses to service of summons (Phase 3 finding 3), and Indiana's
T.R. 6(G) question remains open and parked with Michael.
COMPUTATION STANDARDS are the ones already verified in Phase 3 and unchanged
here: ohio_civ_r_6a and indiana_tr_6a, both of which exclude intermediate
weekends and holidays for periods under seven days. A designated period is
almost always well above seven, but the exclusion remains correctly wired --
it is gated on the counted figure, which for these rules is the designated
one, not the floor.
PRODUCTION-OF-DOCUMENTS RULES (Ohio Civ.R. 34, Ind. T.R. 34) are still not
seeded. They were not read to the same standard and absence means not yet
verified, not verified absent -- the same disclosure made in Phase 5.

rules.label: Answers and objections to interrogatories — period designated by the requesting party (Ohio)

authority.quote: The party upon whom the interrogatories have been served shall serve a copy of the answers and objections within a period designated by the party submitting the interrogatories, not less than twenty-eight days after the service of the interrogatories or within such shorter or longer time as the court may allow.
authority.note: THIS RULE SETS NO DEADLINE. Twenty-eight days is the minimum a valid request may demand; the deadline is whatever the submitting party designated. Supply designated_period_days and the date is computed from that figure. count.value holds 28 only as the floor and is never counted from. The court may also allow a shorter or longer time, quoted above -- the engine has no field for a court order and a computed date here is the request's designated period, not a court-modified one.

rules.label: Answer or objection to a request for admission — period designated in the request (Ohio — unanswered matters are ADMITTED)

authority.quote: within a period designated in the request, not less than twenty-eight days after service
authority.note: Same floor-not-deadline shape as Civ.R. 33(A), and the consequence of missing the designated period is substantive: the matter is ADMITTED, carried in the rule label for that reason. Because the period is designated by the requesting party rather than fixed by the rule, a request designating a short period is exactly the case where the floor check matters -- the engine refuses a below-floor designation rather than computing anything from it.

rules.label: Answers and objections to interrogatories — period designated by the requesting party (Indiana)

authority.quote: The party upon whom the interrogatories have been served shall serve a copy of the answers and objections within a period designated by the party submitting the interrogatories, not less than thirty days after the service thereof or within such shorter or longer time as the court may allow.
authority.note: Indiana's floor is THIRTY days where Ohio's is twenty-eight -- the two rules are near-identical in wording and differ in the number, which is exactly why each was read separately rather than one inferred from the other. Computed under indiana_tr_6a, whose short-period exclusion is gated on the figure actually counted (the designated period), not on the floor.

rules.label: Answer or objection to a request for admission — period designated in the request (Indiana — unanswered matters are ADMITTED)

authority.quote: The matter is admitted unless, within a period designated in the request, not less than thirty days after service thereof or within such shorter or longer time as the court may allow, the party to whom the request is directed serves upon the party requesting the admission a written answer or objection addressed to the matter, signed by the party or by his attorney.
authority.note: Unanswered matters are ADMITTED by operation of the rule, carried in the label. Thirty-day floor, unlike Ohio's twenty-eight. A 2026 amendment noted during Phase 5 research requires requests for admission to be served separately from other discovery -- that is a service-form requirement rather than a timing one and does not affect this computation, but it is recorded here because a future session reading the same source will see it.
